ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in $\odot O(AC>BC)$, with $AB$ being the diameter of $\odot O$. Points E, C, D lie on $\odot O$, and the arcs $\overset{\frown}{EC}=\overset{\frown}{CB}=\overset{\frown}{BD}$. Lines $ED$ intersect $AC, AB$ at points F and G, respectively. $\triangle EFA\sim \triangle BCA$. If $BC=5, BG=4$, calculate the length of $AE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \triangle EFA\sim \triangle BCA$,\\
$\therefore \angle EFA=\angle C=90^\circ$, $\frac{EF}{AE}=\frac{BC}{AB}$,\\
Also $\because \angle CAE=\angle CAB$, $AF=AF$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AEF\cong \triangle AFG$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore AE=AG$, $EF=FG$,\\
$\because \angle AEG=\angle ABD$, $\angle AGE=\angle BGD$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AEG\sim \triangle DBG$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BD}{BG}=\frac{AE}{EG}=\frac{5}{4}$,\\
Let $EF=FG=2x, AE=AG=5x$,\\
$\therefore AB=5x+4$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BC}{AB}=\frac{EF}{AE}=\frac{5}{5x+4}=\frac{2}{5}$,\\
$\therefore x=\frac{17}{10}$,\\
$\therefore AE=5x=\boxed{\frac{17}{2}}$.

method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图中有一个圆，AB 是水平直径，A 在圆的左端，B 在右端，O 在 AB 上接近圆心位置；E 在圆的上方，C 在右上方，D 在右下方。线段 AC 从 A 斜向 C，线 ED 从 E 斜向 D，并与 AC 相交于 F、与 AB 相交于 G。图中 F 位于 AC 与 ED 的交点，G 位于 AB 与 ED 的交点。
推理：因为 AB 是圆 O 的直径，所以由泰勒斯定理，∠ACB = 90°。已知 △EFA ~ △BCA，按对应关系有 ∠EFA = ∠ACB = 90°，且 EF/AE = BC/AB。由于弧 EC = 弧 CB，所以对应的圆周角相等，∠EAC = ∠CAB。又因为 F 在 AC 上，G 在 AB 上，所以 ∠EAF = ∠FAG。并且 E、F、G 共线，EF 垂直 AF，因此 FG 也垂直 AF，∠EFA = ∠AFG = 90°。再加上 AF 公共，所以 △AEF ≅ △AFG，从而 AE = AG，EF = FG。又因为弧 CB = 弧 BD，所以弦 BC = BD；已知 BC = 5，因此 BD = 5。接着看 △AEG 与 △DBG：∠AEG = ∠ABD，因为它们同弧 AD 所对；∠AGE = ∠BGD，为对顶角，所以 △AEG ~ △DBG。因此 AE/EG = BD/BG = 5/4。设 AE = AG = y，则 AB = AG + BG = y + 4。由 AE/EG = 5/4 得 EG = 4y/5。又 EF = FG，且 E、F、G 共线，所以 EG = EF + FG = 2EF，故 EF = 2y/5。代入 EF/AE = BC/AB，得到 2/5 = 5/(y + 4)。解得 y + 4 = 25/2，所以 y = 17/2。因此 AE = 17/2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in $\odot O$ $(AC>BC)$, with $AB$ being the diameter of $\odot O$. Points $E$, $C$, and $D$ lie on $\odot O$, and the arcs $\overset{\frown}{EC}=\overset{\frown}{CB}=\overset{\frown}{BD}$. Lines $ED$ intersect $AC$ and $AB$ at points $F$ and $G$, respectively. $\triangle EFA\sim \triangle BCA$. If $BC=5$ and $BG=4$, calculate the length of $AE$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \triangle EFA\sim \triangle BCA$,\\
$\therefore \angle EFA=\angle C=90^\circ$, $\frac{EF}{AE}=\frac{BC}{AB}$,\\
Also $\because \angle CAE=\angle CAB$, $AF=AF$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AEF\cong \triangle AFG$ (ASA),\\
$\therefore AE=AG$, $EF=FG$,\\
$\because \angle AEG=\angle ABD$, $\angle AGE=\angle BGD$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AEG\sim \triangle DBG$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BD}{BG}=\frac{AE}{EG}=\frac{5}{4}$,\\
Let $EF=FG=2x, AE=AG=5x$,\\
$\therefore AB=5x+4$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BC}{AB}=\frac{EF}{AE}=\frac{5}{5x+4}=\frac{2}{5}$,\\
$\therefore x=\frac{17}{10}$,\\
$\therefore AE=5x=\boxed{\frac{17}{2}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure there is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, A is at the left end of the circle, B is at the right end, and O is on AB near the center of the circle; E is above the circle, C is on the upper right, and D is on the lower right. Segment AC goes obliquely from A to C, line ED goes obliquely from E to D, and intersects AC at F and AB at G. In the figure, F is located at the intersection of AC and ED, and G is located at the intersection of AB and ED.
Reasoning: Because AB is the diameter of circle O, by Thales' theorem, ∠ACB = 90°. It is known that △EFA ~ △BCA, so according to the correspondence there is ∠EFA = ∠ACB = 90°, and EF/AE = BC/AB. Since arc EC = arc CB, the corresponding inscribed angles are equal, ∠EAC = ∠CAB. Also because F is on AC and G is on AB, ∠EAF = ∠FAG. And E, F, G are collinear, EF is perpendicular to AF, therefore FG is also perpendicular to AF, ∠EFA = ∠AFG = 90°. Together with AF common, △AEF ≅ △AFG, thus AE = AG, EF = FG. Also because arc CB = arc BD, chord BC = BD; it is known that BC = 5, therefore BD = 5. Next look at △AEG and △DBG: ∠AEG = ∠ABD, because they subtend the same arc AD; ∠AGE = ∠BGD, being vertical angles, so △AEG ~ △DBG. Therefore AE/EG = BD/BG = 5/4. Let AE = AG = y, then AB = AG + BG = y + 4. From AE/EG = 5/4, get EG = 4y/5. Also EF = FG, and E, F, G are collinear, so EG = EF + FG = 2EF, hence EF = 2y/5. Substitute into EF/AE = BC/AB, obtaining 2/5 = 5/(y + 4). Solving gives y + 4 = 25/2, so y = 17/2. Therefore AE = 17/2.
